# Hardware inventory & first-node selection

## Purpose
Know exactly what hardware exists, in what condition, so the first 3-5 cluster nodes are picked on evidence instead of memory.

## Scope
Gather full hardware stats for all ~12 Threadripper machines (CPU, board, RAM, every NVMe/HDD with model + SMART, NICs, GPUs). Note the 8 HDDs still in the box (no baseline data exists yet). Rank machines by identical-ness and drive quality and name the first 3-5 cluster nodes and their order.

## Execution mode
Hybrid: the inventory design, templates, and analysis are online; gathering stats needs machines powered and reachable (physical), or BMC/KVM access once cabled.

## Dependencies
Feeds every other epic. Node selection gates epics 5 and 6.

## Acceptance
A committed inventory (one record per machine) covering every machine and drive; a named, ordered first-node list with the reasoning recorded; open questions (exact NIC spec, switch gear) either answered or filed as task issues.

---

## EPIC: Basement Talos/Cozystack cluster program

Turn the basement fleet — ~12 Threadripper machines, 15–16 × 16 TB helium HDDs, ≥3 TB DDR4 ECC — into a **3–5 node Talos Linux cluster under Cozystack**, bootstrapped declaratively with TALM, plus the cheap-cloud program around it.

Source of truth: [idea register 2026-10-20](https://github.com/dezren39/hatch-personal/blob/main/workspace/goals/stand-up-lab-cluster-talm-talos-cozystack-postgres-rustfs/files/idea-register-2026-10-20.md) (goal `stand-up-lab-cluster-talm-talos-cozystack-postgres-rustfs`). Research baseline: `hidden_files/research-brief-2026-10-03.md` in the goal (talm v0.35.0, Talos v1.14.1, Cozystack v1.6.4, RustFS 1.0 GA, managed Postgres = CloudNativePG).

### Hard constraints (Drew, explicit)

- **No HashiCorp anything.** Nomad was the plan; the company was sold. All-in on Kubernetes.
- **Everything bootstrappable and declarative.** No undocumented hand-built state — that is why the machines have no OS right now. The fleet must be rebuildable from config in git.
- **Egress is the scarce resource**, not compute: one 2 Gbps symmetric fiber link behind very fast, very cheap local hardware.
- Cloud budget: Turso $5 / Cloudflare $5 Workers plans in play, free tiers preferred, $25–$30 possible later, **$75 out**.

### Day-one cluster services

Postgres (CloudNativePG via Cozystack) · Cloudflare tunnel · Tailscale · NATS · RustFS (S3, cold tiers on HDD pools) · FluxCD running the app directly · DRBD + LINSTOR replication.

### Child issues

- [ ] #1810 — Hardware inventory + hardware-stats gathering: pick the first 3–5 cluster machines (**starts here**: stats decide node order)
- [ ] #1811 — BMC/BIOS configuration audit + routine KVM screenshot verification system
- [ ] #1812 — TALM bootstrap: declarative per-node disk config for non-identical drives
- [ ] #1813 — Storage pools: RAID10 HDD tier for RustFS + striped/mirrored NVMe tiers with LINSTOR/DRBD
- [ ] #1814 — Egress strategy: 2 Gbps home fiber behind Cloudflare/Turso/Tailscale
- [ ] #1816 — OCI always-free maximization: account setup + automation
- [ ] #1815 — Research: boats.dev

### Suggested order

1. #1810 inventory (stats → node shortlist) and #1811 audit groundwork.
2. #1812 TALM proof-of-flow on the first nodes, with #1813 storage design feeding its per-node configs.
3. Cozystack + day-one services on the proven nodes.
4. #1814 egress design before anything user-facing; #1816 OCI in parallel (blocked only on Drew's email/card choice).

### Blockers / open questions for Drew (from the register)

- Basement power capacity + mess: full-fleet power-on is a long tail; 3–5 nodes first.
- Which app does FluxCD run first ("the ID app" — name/repo)?
- OCI account email/card; exact NIC spec + switch gear; boats.dev context; Turso account state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Child issues #1810–#1814 (and any later children) are tracked from this epic with their states kept current.
- [ ] Node selection for the first 3–5 machines is made from #1810's hardware stats and recorded here.
- [ ] The cluster bootstrap is reproducible from config in git (TALM + Talos + Cozystack), with no HashiCorp tooling anywhere in the path.
- [ ] Day-one services from the register (Postgres/CloudNativePG, Cloudflare tunnel, Tailscale, NATS, RustFS, FluxCD, DRBD+LINSTOR) each have a child issue or a recorded deferral.

issue.body:
Drew's directive (2026-10-31): long-term investigation topic — use "Sable uncensored" as the fallback when an API gives a rejection, instead of the request just failing.

This is an INVESTIGATION topic (long-term, staged), not an implementation order. Deliverable is findings + a recommendation; seating anything needs the findings first.

## Problem

Mainstream APIs reject some legitimate work on content-policy grounds — security research and reverse-engineering tooling are the standing fleet examples, alongside adult/creative and controversial-topic work. Today a rejected request simply fails (or worse, in some ecosystems, repeated edgy work puts the account itself at risk). The fleet has no sanctioned lane for work a provider refuses to touch.

## Candidate: "Sable uncensored" — identity UNVERIFIED at filing

First-pass check on 2026-10-31 found NO model or provider named "Sable" in the models.dev / OpenRouter / OpenCode catalogs, and no clear web hit for an uncensored model by that name. Possibilities: a brand-new or niche service, a model id on a specific aggregator, or a dictation artifact for a sound-alike name.

**Deliverable 1 is a positive identification**: provider, model id, endpoint, context window, pricing, tool-calling support, data/retention terms — or a documented finding that no such service exists, with the closest alternatives ranked instead. Alternatives in scope for that ranking (verify, don't assume): Venice AI uncensored models, Cognitive Computations Dolphin builds, hosted abliterated open-weight builds (e.g. UnboundModels' Qwen3.8-27B uncensored), other OpenAI-compatible low-refusal APIs, and self-hosting an abliterated/Dolphin build on fleet hardware.

## Questions the investigation must answer

1. Identity & viability: what is Sable, who runs it, is it still operating, what does it actually serve (weights/build, context window, max output)?
2. Agent fitness: tool calling, structured output, reasoning quality — can it finish real agent work mid-session, or only single-turn text? At what context size?
3. Trigger design: how does the router know a rejection was censorship (error-class shapes per provider)? The companion opencode issue (cross-linked below) covers the other half — censor rejections must never poison route health. This topic covers what the rejected REQUEST does next: fail over to the uncensored lane for that request only.
4. Scope discipline: the uncensored lane is a rejection-triggered special route, NOT a general pool member and never a default. Roles state requirements (Decision 008); this lane's requirement is "the seated models refused this request on content-policy grounds".
5. Privacy & trust: what work may be sent to a niche provider (data terms, retention, training)? Some censored work is censored precisely because it is sensitive.
6. Cost & limits: pricing, rate limits, and whether a free tier exists (relates to the 2026-10-31 free-models investigation: InferX / OpenCode free / alternatives).
7. Bounds: lawful work only; the lane exists for provider over-refusal on legitimate tasks, documented as such.

## Acceptance criteria

- Findings doc: Sable identified or ruled out with evidence; alternatives compared in a table (context, price, tool calls, data terms, quality notes).
- Recommendation: seat / decline / self-host, with reasons, difficulty, and performance considerations.
- If seat: a design sketch for the rejection-triggered route (trigger classification, per-request failover, telemetry) linked to the companion opencode issue — as a follow-up implementation issue, not built from this one.

Companion: developing-today/opencode issue "content-policy (censor) rejections must not count toward model removal, demotion, or disable in routes" (filed 2026-10-31).

issue.body:
## Purpose

Design the **egress** policy for the basement cluster before anything popular lands on it: how traffic splits between Cloudflare, Turso, Tailscale and the direct home link, with a written budget per traffic class. Child of #1091 (cloud extension — egress half); absorbs #1814, which carried this content but had no home in the program structure.

**The constraint:** bandwidth is the scarce resource, not compute. The basement fleet has very fast CPUs, ≥3 TB RAM and ~200 TB of disks at near-zero marginal cost — behind exactly **2 Gbps symmetric** home fiber.

Source: idea register 2026-10-20 (goal `stand-up-lab-cluster-talm-talos-cozystack-postgres-rustfs`), plus the superseded #1814 body.

## What we know

- One fiber provider (Brightspeed) in his part of Osseo: 2 Gbps up/down. A second line = 4 Gbps total — still small at scale. Cable offers 100 Mbps, more expensive (possible redundancy pickup). TriCounty Communications fiber may reach his part of Osseo → then buy both fibers.
- Hotspot plans and Starlink investigated for emergency backup; Starlink would likely need a business plan for this use.
- Strategy direction (Drew): "tunnel most or much of that to Cloudflare or Turso or anywhere we connect with Tailscale" — shunt bulk traffic to SaaS with cheap or **free egress** (e.g. Cloudflare R2's zero-egress pricing, CF cache/tunnels), compress aggressively, and only cross the home link with what must.
- Budget guardrails: Turso $5 plan and Cloudflare $5 Workers plan in play; free tiers preferred; a $25–$30 Cloudflare plan is possible; **$75 is out**.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Classify the app's traffic: what can be cached at the edge (CDN), what can live on free-egress object storage (R2), what genuinely must be served from home.
- [ ] Design the tunnel topology: cloudflared from the cluster, Tailscale links, Turso edge replicas — with per-path egress costs written down.
- [ ] Compression plan per traffic class (static assets, API payloads, media) and the CPU cost of doing it on the Threadrippers (plenty available).
- [ ] Failure/redundancy matrix: fiber cut, cable fallback (100 Mbps — what degrades, in what order), Starlink/hotspot emergency tier.
- [ ] Output: a one-page egress budget model — expected GB/month per class vs the ~2 Gbps link and each SaaS allowance — kept current in the subscription/usage ledger.
- [ ] Design recorded on this issue or a linked design doc/PR, stating the bandwidth budget against the 2 Gbps symmetric constraint and what happens when it is exceeded.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation issues filed and linked for any build work the design calls for.

## Open questions

- Is TriCounty fiber actually available at the address? (Needs an address check.)
- Which SaaS egress allowances are we already paying for but not using (ties into the cloud ideation ledger)?

issue.body:
Part of the basement cluster program #1817 / network fabric #1084; egress/tunnel topology context in #5030. Drew approved 2026-11-06 ("we've used tunnels here before. go ahead. Use CF versions and/or nix flake to handle deploy / service").

State found (verified 2026-11-06 via the Cloudflare API, two reads):
- The account has exactly ONE existing tunnel: `amd-6-pm-stack` (healthy), remotely managed, ingress kaneo.security.cab + dispatch.security.cab -> localhost services on amd, connector = the `pm-tunnel` home-manager user service in nixos/services/pm-stack (cloudflared from the flake, `--protocol http2` per #5647). The 2026-11-05 "zero tunnels" prep note was wrong — the established pattern below is what this issue follows.
- The only DNS zone in the account is security.cab.
- The lab cluster hardware is not stood up yet (#1086 depends on the physical bring-up under #6066), so the first lab connector runs on amd — the always-on NixOS host — exactly where the pm-stack connector already runs.

Work:
- Create a second, separate remotely-managed tunnel `lab-cluster` (config source: Cloudflare), token vaulted in BWS as `cloudflare.tunnel.lab-cluster-token`.
- Seed ingress: `lab.security.cab` -> a small lab edge status service on amd loopback (127.0.0.1:8790), catch-all 404 — the seed endpoint future lab services (Cozystack dashboard, BMC broker per the ideas log) join as they land. CNAME lab.security.cab -> <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com (proxied) in the security.cab zone.
- Deploy/service in the flake: new module `nixos/services/lab-tunnel/` modeled on pm-stack's pm-tunnel (home-manager user services, cloudflared from nixpkgs, `--protocol http2 --no-autoupdate run --token` with the token in an operator-rendered EnvironmentFile ~/lab-tunnel/tunnel.env, never in git), wired into the amd host profiles + enable, through a PR.
- Interim activation until the next switch: transient user units on amd (cleanly reversible), replaced by the flake units at switch time.
- Verify end-to-end from outside the house network path (sandbox egress): https://lab.security.cab returns the status page, twice independently.

Next step after this issue (documented, not built here): the redundant second connector — same tunnel, second host (first lab node when it lands, or the spare tunnel host from the BMC-broker idea) — Cloudflare load-balances connectors on one tunnel automatically.

Access note: the seed status page is non-sensitive and public like kaneo/dispatch. Any real lab UI (BMC/KVM, Cozystack) gets Cloudflare Access in front when it is added, per the ideas-log design.
